To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal conductivity and mechanical behavior of metal matrix diamond particle composites are strongly affected by interfacial thermal and elastic conductivities.

(a) the thermal conductivity of diamond reinforced metal matrix composites is governed by the particle shapes and interfacial conductance, (b) the effective elastic moduli and yield stress of the composites are governed by the particle shape and interfacial properties, (c) the effective yield stress of the composite is significantly lower than the yield stress of the matrix, and (d) the effective thermal conductivity and effective yield stress of diamond reinforced metals are significantly affected by the presence of the diamond particles

(a) the thermal conductivity of diamond reinforced compositess is strongly influenced by the interfacial conductance between the matrix and reinforcement, (b) the thermal conductivity is significantly affected by the diamond particle shape and orientation, and (c) the elastic and thermomechanically induced plasticity of diamond reinforced metals is influenced by the diamond particle orientation and shape.
In summary, our research is concerned with
modeling of the effective thermal and thermomechanics behavior of composites reinforced by hard particles.
the modeling of the thermal and thermomechanically induced behavior of metal matrix diamond composites, including the effects of finite interface conductances and particle shape.
the modeling of the thermal conductivity as well as the thermomechanical response of diamond reinforced metal matrix composites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the thermal conductivity of metal matrix composite reinforced by diamond particles is mainly governed by the interfacial conductance, while the elastic and thermoelastic-plastic behavior is mainly governed by particle shape and size.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of semi-analytical methods and numerical simulations is very useful for the study of the overall thermal and mechanical behavior of metal matrix nanocomposites.
the Mori–Tanaka method is a very useful tool for the analysis of metal matrix composite materials, especially when the interphase between the matrix and reinforcements is considered.

a combination of semi-analytical methods and numerical simulations provides an efficient way to predict the thermal conductivity and the mechanical behavior of metal matrix composite materials reinforced with diamond particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a given particle volume fraction, the effective thermal conductivity of diamond reinforced composite materials is not only a function of the thermal conductivity of the constituents, but is also strongly dependent on the shape, size and orientation distribution of the reinforcing particles.
the Mori–Tanaka method can be used as a powerful and efficient tool in predicting the thermal and thermomechanics of composites reinforced by high thermal conductivity particles.

the overall thermal and thermomechanic properties of metal matrix composite can be accurately predicted using a combination of analytical and numerical methods, provided that the thermal contact conductance is taken into account.
